For instance, after "Initial Interviews," the Opuwo Rural Women 18-25 group further declines to 200, whereas Windhoek Urban Men 26-35 reduce to 550 individuals.

By the "Hired" stage, the number of individuals across all groups significantly decreases, with the Opuwo Rural Women 18-25 group having the lowest at 10 individuals and Windhoek Urban Men 26-35 the highest at 100 individuals. The retention stages show minimal further reductions, indicating stability among those who have secured employment. At the one-year retention mark, the numbers are relatively low across all groups, with Windhoek Urban Men 26-35 retaining the highest at 85 individuals and Opuwo Rural Women 18-25 the lowest at 5 individuals.

The chart effectively highlights disparities in employment progression among different demographic groups in Namibian regions, illustrating how various factors such as region, gender, and age may influence employment outcomes.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
source = source.replace(
    "plt.title('Employment Pipeline",
    "plt.plot(df['Stage'], df['Opuwo Rural Women 18-25'], marker='o', label='Opuwo Rural Women 18-25', color=colors[-1])\n\nplt.title('Employment Pipeline",
    1
)
source = source.replace("plt.ylabel('Average Time in Stage (Days)', labelpad=10)",
                        "plt.ylabel('Number of Individuals', labelpad=10)")
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
plt.close('all')
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
print("TABLE:\n", table.to_string(index=False))
print("Y-axis:", ax.get_ylabel())
print("Series:", ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1])
print("Number of lines:", len(ax.lines))
print("Y limits:", ax.get_ylim())
for line in ax.lines:
    name = line.get_label()
    assert list(line.get_ydata()) == list(df[name])
assert len(ax.lines) == 12
assert ax.get_ylabel() == "Number of Individuals"
